reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous pattern recognition with robust XAI tools to detect shared spurious features. The autonomous analysis identifies commonalities across misclassified instances, such as shared demographic and relational attributes, while XAI tools provide quantitative attribution scores to validate which features drive misclassifications despite lacking semantic relevance. This dual approach increases accuracy in detecting spurious correlations.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify the exact feature values that are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 35024) and evaluate whether any feature is universally present and potentially spurious.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features and their values across the instances, highlighting any non-semantic or potentially spurious attributes

autonomous_tasks.query: Assess whether the shared features (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, occupation=Craft-repair/Sales/Other-service, education=HS-grad) could be spurious correlates due to demographic bias or data collection artifacts, especially when they do not directly relate to income class.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned explanation of whether shared features may be spurious despite their prevalence

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides global feature importance with intersection-based comparison to identify features that are high in all misclassified instances. LIME offers local interpretability to validate how each feature contributes in specific instances. Integrated Gradients calculate gradients along a path to zero, revealing attribution strength, while sensitivity analysis quantifies the impact of removing each feature. Together, these tools confirm whether shared features exhibit high attribution despite lacking semantic relevance.
